topicName: Database Migrations and Zero-Downtime Schema Changes
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Database Migrations and Zero-Downtime Schema Changes"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Deploying application code alongside database schema changes without causing downtime is one of the most critical challenges in backend engineering. A poorly planned migration can lock tables, exhaust connection pools, or break running application instances."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"The Expand and Contract Pattern"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"To achieve zero-downtime deployments, you must decouple schema changes from code deployment. The industry standard approach is the Expand and Contract pattern, also known as the Parallel Run pattern. This involves three distinct phases: Expand, Migrate, and Contract."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Expand: Add new database structures (tables, columns) while keeping old ones operational."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Migrate: Deploy application code that writes to both old and new structures, and backfill historical data."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Contract: Remove old structures and legacy application code once migration is fully verified."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Step-by-Step Example: Renaming a Column Safely"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Imagine you need to rename a column 'first_name' to 'given_name' in a high-traffic 'users' table. Executing an immediate ALTER TABLE rename will lock the table and break running application queries expecting 'first_name'."},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Phase 1: Expand. Add the new column without enforcing NOT NULL constraints immediately."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN given_name VARCHAR(255);"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Phase 2: Dual Write. Update your application code to write to both 'first_name' and 'given_name' simultaneously, while still reading primarily from 'first_name'."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"UPDATE users SET first_name = 'John', given_name = 'John' WHERE id = 1;"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Phase 3: Backfill. Run a background script to copy historical data from the old column to the new column in small, throttled batches to avoid locking the database."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"UPDATE users SET given_name = first_name WHERE given_name IS NULL LIMIT 1000;"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Phase 4: Switch Reads. Update the application to read exclusively from 'given_name'."},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Phase 5: Contract. Drop the old column and remove the dual-write logic from the application codebase."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN first_name;"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Safe Migrations"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid long-running transactions that hold exclusive locks on heavily queried tables."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Set strict statement timeouts and lock timeouts to prevent migration scripts from hanging indefinitely."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always ensure your migrations are backward-compatible so that older application instances can run against the updated schema temporarily during rolling deployments."}]
